records.section_heading: American Samoa Territorial Monitoring Program Manu'a Reef Flat Baseline Surveys, February 2015.
records.question: How many reef flat sites were surveyed around the islands of Ofu and Olosega during the Manu'a baseline surveys in February 2015?
ground_truth_chunks: Surveys were conducted at 12 sites around the islands of Ofu and Olosega as shown by the red lines in figures 1 and 2 (GPS coordinates for each of the sites are listed in Appendix 1).
The aim of these surveys was to conduct baseline surveys from which to detect temporal change if it should occur.

records.question: Which survey site had the highest percent crustose coralline algae (CCA) in Table 2?
records.ground_truth_answer: Pool 600 had the highest CCA at 25 ± 8.4%.

records.question: Which transect had the highest mean fish biomass and what was its mean biomass?
records.ground_truth_answer: Pool 400A, with a mean biomass of 46.8 g/m-2 (69% of the biomass attributed to herbivorous fish).
ground_truth_chunks: Overall, the highest mean fish biomass were recorded within the National Park boundary between Pool 300 and Pool 600.
The highest mean fish biomass was recorded at Pool 400A with a mean biomass of 46.8 g/m-2 , of which 69% of the total biomass along this transect was attributed to herbivorous fish.

records.question: Which pool had the highest coral cover?
records.ground_truth_answer: Pool 300 had the highest coral cover, at 24%.
ground_truth_chunks: Overall, Pool 100B, 200C, 300, 400A and 600 had the highest coral cover (19-24%). Highest coral cover was found in Pool 300 (24%) (Table 2 and Figure 6).
